title: Generic constancy of the number of geometric irreducible components
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For each $t\in Y$, write $X_t$ for its scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], over the residue field $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and choose a separable closure $\kappa(t)^s$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. Count the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X_t\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)^s$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every $y\in Y$ there are a nonempty relatively open subset $V\subseteq\overline{\{y\}}$ and an integer $n\geq0$ such that this number is exactly $n$ for every $t\in V$. The assertion holds for any choices of the separable closures; no flatness or Noetherian hypothesis on $f$ or $Y$ is required.

source.place: Tag 055A (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-good), with the geometric-component-count convention of Tag 0556 (lemma-base-change-fibres-nr-geometrically-irreducible-components). Finite type makes each geometric fibre Noetherian, so the constant value is a finite nonnegative integer.

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$ and let $S$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{\{y\}}$. Its underlying space is this closure and has generic point $y$: the closure of a point is irreducible, since if it is covered by two closed subsets, the one containing the point contains its closure. Form $h:X_S=X\times_Y S\to S$. This is finite type by base-change stability. The base-change count theorem gives $n_{X_S/S}=n_{X/Y}|_S$ and independence from all separably closed extensions. It therefore suffices to find a nonempty open of $S$ on which this function has one finite value. In the remaining steps rename $X_S,S,h,y$ as $X,S,h,\eta$; thus $S$ is irreducible and $\eta$ is its generic point.

Put $k=\kappa(\eta)$. Apply [lem-trf-generic-split-component-upper-bound] to $h:X\to S$. It supplies a finite etale generic field extension $L/k$ with spectrum map $a$, a finite component count $n\geq0$ for $G=X_\eta\times_k\operatorname{Spec}L$, and an open $W$ containing $\eta$ on which every field-extended fibre has at most $n$ components. In particular $n_{X/S}(s)\leq n$ for $s\in W$.

source.place: Tag 055A (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-good), proof, generic splitting and geometric upper bound.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-generic-component-lower-bound] with the same $L,a,n,G$: Step 2 supplies its finite etale field map and exactly $n$ ordinary components of $G$. It gives an irreducible scheme $T$, an etale $g:T\to S$, a generic point $\xi$ above $\eta$, and an open $U$ containing $\xi$. For $P=X\times_S T$, the compatible residue-field isomorphism identifies $P_\xi$ with $G$, and every field extension of every fibre over $U$ has at least $n$ components. Taking separable closures gives $n_{P/T}(t)\geq n$ on $U$.

source.place: Tag 055A (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-good), proof, etale model and ordinary-to-geometric lower bound.

proof.text: Let $U_0=U\cap g^{-1}(W)$. It contains $\xi$, because $g(\xi)=\eta\in W$, so it is nonempty and open. Etale openness shows that $V=g(U_0)$ is a nonempty open subset of $S$ contained in $W$; it contains $\eta=g(\xi)$. For every $s\in V$ choose $t\in U_0$ with $g(t)=s$. By base-change invariance, $n_{X/S}(s)=n_{P/T}(t)\geq n$; by Step 2, $n_{X/S}(s)\leq n$. Thus it equals the finite integer $n$. Step 1 identifies $V$ with a relatively open nonempty subset of the original $\overline{\{y\}}$ and identifies the component-count functions there. Independence from all choices of separable closure was included in Step 1, and no flatness or Noetherian hypothesis was added.
